chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he recited this Verse:
But! The human being is evidence against himself * Although he puts forth his excuses
O Abu Hafs! The human being cannot get closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by going against what Allah the Exalted Knows.

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: 'The one who does a secretive deed, Allah would Return it with a Returning - if it was good, so good, and if it was evil, so evil'.
ai.seo_question: How does concealing one's deeds affect one's closeness to God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *ikhlas* (sincerity) by contrasting outward performance with inner alignment to Divine knowledge, citing the verse 'Man is a witness against himself' (75:14-15). The Imam highlights the Prophet’s teaching that God repays a secret deed with its inherent nature, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the unity of the inner and outer self in worship. This context underscores that true piety requires one's hidden state to match one's revealed actions, avoiding the spiritual dissonance of showing off.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,
‘I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when he<sup>asws</sup> recited this Verse
[75:14] But! The human being is evidence against himself [75:15] Although he puts forth his excuses.
O Abu Hafs! The human being cannot get closer to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic by going against what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Knows.
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘The one who does a secretive deed, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Return it with a Returning - if it was good, so good, and if it was evil, so evil’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:
“Once I was having dinner with abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and he read this verse of the Holy Quran:
‘In fact, people are well-aware of their own soul [75:14] even though they make excuses.’ [75:15]

The Imam said, ‘O abu Hafs, why should a human being seek closeness (by the form of the deed) to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, while it is against the knowledge of Allah (in one’s intention being to show off)?
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever does a deed secretly, Allah returns it in a certain dress, as good rewards, were it a good deed, and in an evil form, were it an evil deed.’”
